trip_note: 9 days, early March 2027, ~5 friends flying from Buenos Aires. Lima 2 nights (Barranco) + Mancora 5 nights + Lima transit home. All prices are USD. Hotel per-person prices assume 2 sharing a double; Airbnb per-person prices assume 5 sharing. NO price below is a confirmed March-2027 quote: none of these properties publish rates 18 months out. Every price is the current (Sept 2026) rate seen on Booking.com, the hotel's own site or an OTA, so every hotel is marked is_estimate true. Early March is HIGH season on the north coast (Peruvian summer), so budget +15-30% over the figures shown.

stops.name: Lima
stops.area_note: Barranco is the right call for this group: clifftop, walkable, street art, Hotel B / MATE / Pedro de Osma / Central / Kjolle / Isolina / Merito / Lady Bee all inside ~15 blocks, and the Miraflores malecon is a 25-min walk or 10-min taxi north. Miraflores is safer-feeling and has more hotel stock but is comparatively corporate. Airport (LIM) to Barranco is 45-70 min depending on traffic; use an official airport taxi or Uber/Cabify, roughly USD 20-30. HONESTY FLAG: Booking.com individual hotel pages could not be fetched directly (they return empty to automated fetches) - scores and prices below come from Booking.com's Barranco district and Lima design-hotel listing pages fetched 2026-09-20, plus hotel official sites. Two of the five Barranco booking URLs could not be confirmed as exact slugs, so a Booking.com search URL is given instead and flagged.

stops.weather_note: Early March is the tail of Lima's summer and the best weather of the year: highs around 26-28C, nights around 19-20C, high humidity (70-85%), very strong UV, and essentially no rain - Lima is a coastal desert and the grey garua drizzle is a May-October thing, not March. The sea is at its annual warmest but the Humboldt current still keeps it cool, roughly 20-22C, so the malecon beaches are swimmable-but-bracing rather than tropical. HONESTY: the web-search budget ran out before a Lima March climate page could be fetched, so these figures come from general climate knowledge rather than a source fetched in this pass - sanity-check on weather-and-climate.com or senamhi.gob.pe before packing.

stops.name: Mancora (Piura / Tumbes north coast)
stops.area_note: The strip runs roughly north to south: Punta Sal / Canoas (25-45 min north, wide and calm, family-ish) - Mancora town (the party and the point break) - Las Pocitas (2km south, rock tide pools, the boutique hotels) - Vichayito (a further 5-10 min south, emptiest sand, whole-house rentals) - Los Organos (10-15 min south, fishing village, the advanced left called La Vuelta) - El Nuro (the turtle pier) - Cabo Blanco (40 min south, Hemingway's old fishing club and a world-class barrel on north swells). LAS POCITAS AND VICHAYITO ARE THE RIGHT BASE for this group: beautiful, quiet, and a S/5-15 mototaxi from Mancora's restaurants and bars, so you get the scene without sleeping in it. GETTING THERE from Lima: fly LIM to Talara (TYL, ~1h from Mancora), Tumbes (TBP, ~1h30) or Piura (PIU, ~2h30); LATAM and Sky fly all three. Pre-book a private transfer (roughly USD 40-60 for the car from Talara) or share a colectivo. HONESTY FLAG: Booking.com individual hotel pages return empty to automated fetches, so scores and prices below come from Booking.com's Mancora, Vichayito, Los Organos and Canoas de Punta Sal city listing pages plus the Mancora design-hotels page, all fetched 2026-09-20, cross-checked against hotel official sites. Where the exact Booking.com slug could not be confirmed, a Booking.com search URL is given and flagged.

Mancora point works essentially year-round at 1-2.5m and gets crowded. Schools: Mancora Kite Club, Surf Point Mancora, Inca Warriors.

activities.what: Sulfurous thermal mud pool up the Fernandez valley, 11km inland, reached by mototaxi.
activities.note: VERIFIED: entrance S/5-15 (USD 1.50-4) if you go alone by mototaxi (~35 min each way). Organised tours with hotel pickup, mototaxi transfer, guide and the Mirador viewpoint run roughly USD 25-35 pp and last 2h30. You can also reach it on horseback (2h) or on foot (4h). GetYourGuide/Civitatis product pages return 403 to automated fetches so the tour price is a range estimate.

activities.note: VERIFIED price: TraviTour lists the coastal horse ride at S/60 list, S/40 sale (USD 11-17). Finca Capitan Mancora (fincacapitanmancora.com) also runs guided rides. Book the day before; the sunset slot fills.

activities.name: Swim with green sea turtles at El Nuro pier
activities.what: Wild green turtles gather under the fishing pier for scraps; you snorkel among them from a small boat.
activities.when: Morning, 08:00-11:00 (pier open 08:00-17:00, calmest and clearest early)
activities.note: VERIFIED DIY cost: pier entry S/5, swim-with-turtles boat S/10-15, compulsory life jacket S/2, optional snorkel S/5 - about USD 6-8 all in, plus mototaxi/colectivo from Mancora (20km, ~S/15-25). Organised 3-hour tours from Mancora start around S/100 (USD 27) and go up to USD 45 for catamaran versions. SEASON HONESTY: one regional guide lists 'sea turtle swimming: June-Oct', but the El Nuro turtles are resident year-round because they follow the fishing boats - most operators run this daily all year. Confirm with your hotel the week before.

activities.name: Lunch in Los Organos and the La Vuelta left
activities.what: Fishing-village lunch, then watch (or surf) the powerful tubular left reef called La Vuelta.
activities.note: SEASON: VERIFIED GOOD FOR MARCH. La Vuelta works on north swells, October to April, up to 2.5m with multiple tube sections - described as one of the best waves in Peru. Advanced only; beginners should watch, not paddle out.

activities.name: Day trip north to Punta Sal / Canoas
activities.what: The strip's widest, calmest, emptiest beach, 25-45 min north in the Tumbes region.
activities.note: Colectivo along the Panamericana runs roughly S/10-15 each way (USD 3-4); a private taxi for five is around USD 40-60 return. Lunch on the beach USD 15-25. If you want to stay a night, El Samay Hotel Boutique in Canoas de Punta Sal scores 9.8/10 on Booking.com across ~220 reviews at about USD 100/night (USD 50 pp) - the best value-per-quality on the whole coast.

activities.name: Cabo Blanco: Hemingway's fishing club and the barrel
activities.what: Forty minutes south; the 1950s big-game fishing club site and a world-famous tubing left.
activities.note: TWO HONESTY FLAGS. (1) SURF: verified good for March - Cabo Blanco is a left reef break working on north swells October to April, up to 3m, 'world famous for its long, perfect tubes', but it only truly breaks around 8 times a year and is advanced-only. (2) DEEP-SEA FISHING: Cabo Blanco is NO LONGER an organised sportfishing destination. Hemingway fished here in 1956 and Alfred Glassell's 1,560lb black marlin world record still stands from 1953, but current sources describe basic facilities and limited organised charters - you negotiate directly with local boats. Expect USD 250-450 for a boat for the day, cash, arranged through your hotel. Peru-wide charters on FishingBooker start around USD 245. NONE OF THIS IS A CONFIRMED QUOTE.

activities.name: Kitesurfing lesson - ONLY IF THE WIND SHOWS UP
activities.what: Mobile schools cover Mancora, Pocitas, Vichayito, Los Organos and El Nuro and come to your hotel.
activities.when: Afternoon, 11:00-17:00 when the thermal wind builds
activities.note: SEASON HONESTY - MARCH IS THE WRONG MONTH. Verified: the Mancora kite season runs roughly April/May to December, with the most constant wind in August, September and October. Early March is at the bottom of the wind cycle. Keep this as an opportunistic 'if it is blowing' item, not a planned day. VERIFIED prices when it does run: USD 245 for a 6-hour semi-private beginner course, USD 360 for 3 afternoons of private lessons; a local guide quotes S/200-350 for single lessons.

activities.name: Last-day slow plan: SUP or snorkel, then sunset drinks in Mancora
activities.what: Paddleboard the flat Vichayito water in the morning, then the Mancora beach bars for sunset.
activities.note: SUP rental roughly S/40-60/hour (USD 11-16) from hotels along Vichayito and Pocitas. Mancora's beach bars are lively but not a party-hostel scene before ~22:00; after that the main drag gets loud.

activities.name: WHALE WATCHING - NOT AVAILABLE IN MARCH
activities.what: Humpbacks migrating from Antarctica to calve off Los Organos, Punta Sal and Mancora.
activities.note: CLEAR NO. Multiple independent sources confirm the season starts mid-July and ends late October. Early March is four months outside it and there will be no humpbacks. Listed here only so nobody in the group books a March 'whale tour' from an operator happy to take the money. When it does run it costs S/80-150 (USD 22-40) for 2-3 hours from Los Organos. Day 0 is a deliberate marker, not a trip day.

stops.weather_note: March is Mancora's hottest month and the best swimming of the year: daytime highs around 30-31C (the national weather service puts the March average high at 30.8C), nights around 23-24C, sea temperature around 25C - the warmest it gets - and about 10.6 hours of sun a day. December to April is the peak beach season, so early March is hot, sunny and BUSY, with high-season room rates. THE HONEST CAVEAT: March is also statistically the wettest month on the north coast, averaging around 128mm of rain. That average is heavily skewed by El Nino years; in a normal year you get a handful of short, heavy afternoon downpours and high humidity rather than washed-out days, but it is not a guaranteed-dry month the way August is. Pack for heat and humidity, bring reef-safe sunscreen, and do not count on five consecutive cloudless days.

getting_around: MANCORA: mototaxis (tuk-tuks) are the whole transport system and they are everywhere. Verified fares: S/2-5 (USD 0.50-1.30) within Mancora town; S/5-10 to Las Pocitas; S/10-15 to Vichayito; S/15-25 to Los Organos or El Nuro. Always agree the fare before you get in - prices move with demand and time of day, and after midnight they roughly double. Colectivos (shared vans) run up and down the Panamericana for S/3-8 and are how you get to Punta Sal or Cabo Blanco cheaply. Bicycle rental is S/20-30 a day; motorbike rental exists but the highway is fast and badly lit. Mancora town itself is walkable end to end in about 15 minutes. From Las Pocitas you can walk to town along the beach at low tide in 25-30 minutes. Several Pocitas and Vichayito hotels run their own shuttles - ask, it is often free. AIRPORTS: Talara (TYL) ~1h, Tumbes (TBP) ~1h30, Piura (PIU) ~2h30; a private transfer from Talara is roughly USD 40-60 for the car, and companies like Texa Tours and Talara Express do airport-to-beach runs. LIMA: use Uber, Cabify or DiDi rather than street taxis; Barranco to Miraflores is USD 4-7, Barranco to the airport USD 20-30 and 45-70 minutes depending on traffic. Barranco itself is entirely walkable and the Miraflores malecon is a flat 10km cycle path.
